note: DATA, NOT CODE. Every field here is read by plugins/mod/hooks/guard.ts and by `jq` — ops extends this list without a plugin release. Each entry names the CLAUDE.md rule it replaces; a policy with no `rule` is not a policy, it is a preference.

policies.rule: Test fixtures: never a real identifier (5dive/CLAUDE.md)

checks.say: a Telegram id that is not the reserved fake 1234567890
an IP address outside the RFC 5737 documentation range 192.0.2.x

policies.deny: This writes {found} into a test fixture ({path}). The rule is a NAMED DEFAULT, not more care: Telegram ids are 1234567890, emails are @example.com, IP addresses are 192.0.2.x (RFC 5737). Change the value, do not change the path. [{rule}]

policies.rule: The pre-push PII guard catches these; do not --no-verify past it (5dive/CLAUDE.md)

checks.say: a git commit or push with --no-verify

policies.deny: {found} skips the pre-push PII guard and the co-author hook — the two rails that grade what this repo will CONTAIN. If a hook is wrong, fix the hook or say on the row why it is wrong; bypassing it leaves no record that it was bypassed. [{rule}]

policies.rule: Never apply smoke-verified when the smoke did not run — that is forging an attestation (5dive/CLAUDE.md)
policies.deny: {found}. That label asserts the paid Hetzner smoke ran green at this sha, and only the smoke can produce it — the other exit is `smoke-override` with the five-part written reason. If the smoke DID run, record its sha in the seat's FIVEDIVE_MOD_GUARD_SMOKE_RECEIPT setting first, so the attestation has an author. [{rule}]

policies.rule: The audit log and the runtime store are append-only to the runtime, not to a seat (mod guard, capability 2)

checks.say: a write into the runtime's own store or audit log

policies.deny: {found} ({path}). The runtime owns these paths: a row, a gate and an audit line are written through `5dive`, which records who wrote them. A direct write leaves a state the CLI did not make and cannot explain. [{rule}]

policies.rule: Destructive commands stay inside the workdir (mod guard, capability 2)

checks.say: a `git clean -f`, which deletes another seat's uncommitted work when the checkout is shared

policies.deny: {found}. Outside your own worktree these paths belong to the host or to another seat, and the delete is not revertible by a redeploy. Name the directory you mean, or do it from your worktree. [{rule}]

policies.rule: A reply on a repo we do not own goes out as lodar; it needs a per-thread approval (main's identity-cap rule)

checks.say: a public reply on a repository owned by {match}

policies.deny: {found}. This seat's GitHub token writes under an identity that is not yours, so the comment is published in someone else's name on a project we do not own — it cannot be unsent. Put the text on the row and get the one-line approval first. [{rule}]
